newsitem.title: GERMANY: German media hail damning report on Swiss WW2 - role.
newsitem.headline: German media hail damning report on Swiss WW2 - role.

text.p: German media have applauded a U.S. State Department report that criticised Switzerland for banking Nazi gold during World War Two.

The U.S. report, published on Wednesday, said there was no evidence Swiss officials knew that gold they bought had been salvaged from the jewellery, even the teeth, of Jews who perished in Holocaust extermination camps.
But it asserted they did know they bought gold taken from treasuries of Nazi-occupied countries.

"The dark shadow of entanglement is falling across countries which tried to avoid being drawn into Nazi Germany's war by claiming they were -- rather than actually being -- neutral," The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung daily said on Friday.
"By having done its best to avoid handing back the gold, Switzerland falls into the category of war-profiteers," the daily Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper said in a commentary.

Newspapers cheered the report for rapping the United States over its failure to push the Swiss hard enough at the end of the war to account for and return millions of dollars worth of gold acquired in wartime financial deals with the Nazis.
"It is not always easy to say where the border is between the morally justified drive for self-preservation and economic exploitation of a conflict," the Frankfurter Rundschau said.
"But the report leaves not doubt that Bern's motives were of an economic rather than political nature," it said.
Germany has had little to do with tracking down Nazi gold so far, as the bulk of Nazi central bank records were confiscated by the U.S. forces after the war and only a few fragments remained here.
A Finance Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday Bonn had put the Bundesbank archive at researchers' disposal and that it had pledged its support to institutions involved in the search.

Marvin Hier, head of a California organisation which pursues Holocaust culprits, said this week that the German government had given him its word that it would probe what happened to the personal wealth of hundreds of leading Nazis.

The U.S. report said the Reichsbank, Nazi Germany's central bank, had an account for melted-down loot from death camp victims, such as rings, coins and even gold teeth, and sold some of this along with gold taken from occupied countries to finance the German war machine.

It also said that at least a small portion of the gold that entered Switzerland and Italy included non-monetary gold from individual civilians in occupied countries and from concentration camp victims or others killed before they even reached the camps.
But it stopped short of calling for reopening post-war accords in order to seek more reparations from the Swiss.

A spokesman for the Swiss government said Bern was shocked by news of the report that took seven months to complete and U.S. Jewish groups welcomed it and said Switzerland would now be obliged to address their material claims.
